question.problem:
A random variable $X$ has the probability distribution given below.

| $x$ | $0$ | $5$ | $10$ | $15$ | $20$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $\frac{1}{4}$ | $\frac{1}{8}$ | $\frac{1}{4}$ | $\frac{1}{8}$ | $\frac{1}{4}$ |

Calculate $\text{E}[-\frac{3}{2}X-5].$
question.worked_solution:
First, let's find $\text{E}[X].$ 

The expected value of a discrete random variable $X$ with probability mass function $f(x)$ and sample space $S$ is given by

$$
\text{E}[X]={\sum }_{x\in S}x\cdot f(x).
$$

Summing up the products of each value of $X$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\sum }_{x\in S}x\cdot f(x) \\  & =0\cdot \frac{1}{4}+5\cdot \frac{1}{8}+10\cdot \frac{1}{4}+15\cdot \frac{1}{8}+20\cdot \frac{1}{4} \\  & =10.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[-\frac{3}{2}X-5] & =-\frac{3}{2}\text{E}[X]-5 \\  & =-\frac{3}{2}\cdot 10-5 \\  & =-20.\end{aligned}
$$
